findings.desc: CHK-001:happy:0 and CHK-001:adversarial:0 are bound to evidence commands that do not directly exercise the toOwnPropsNullProto chokepoint or the pollution surface for those intents. CHK-001:happy:0 cites usage-ledger-adapter-smoke.js (a pre-existing round-trip smoke that does not call toOwnPropsNullProto directly or assert Object.getPrototypeOf===null). CHK-001:adversarial:0 cites usage-ledger-codex-gemini-smoke.js (codex/gemini path smoke, not the whitelist-drop or null-proto property assertions). The intent text explicitly requires asserting null-prototype and whitelist-drop behavior. The pollution smoke (usage-ledger-prototype-pollution-smoke.js) does assert these via checks 1-4 (helper direct tests) and checks 5/8/10 (billing preserved), but neither of the cited commands drives those assertions. This is a command-to-intent binding mismatch per the evidence-must-bind-literal-intent-command rule.
findings.resolvedReason: Re-recorded CHK-001:happy:0 + adversarial:0 (and all 9) bound to the smoke command that actually drives them (ef73b51).

findings.desc: CHK-003:adversarial:0 evidence note honestly discloses that the estimate path pollution assertion (check 17 in the smoke, labeled LOAD-BEARING) passes even pre-hardening by design, because the estimate path computes inputTokens from prompt bytes and sets output/cache to literal null — it never reads any token key off an externally-derived usage object. However, the smoke labels this check LOAD-BEARING in the check label string itself (line 353: estimate (LOAD-BEARING): ...). This label is inaccurate at the source level: a reader inspecting the smoke code sees a LOAD-BEARING label for an assertion that the evidence note concedes is not load-bearing. The CHK-003:adversarial:0 intent requires ALL pollution assertions to be load-bearing. The evidence note provides accurate disclosure but the smoke label creates a contradiction that must be resolved: either remove the LOAD-BEARING label from check 17 and add a clear NOT-LOAD-BEARING annotation, or remove the check from the load-bearing count and add an advisory note in the smoke. The current state where the code says LOAD-BEARING and the note says it is not is a honesty gap.
findings.resolvedReason: Estimate-path smoke check relabeled honestly (NOT load-bearing) in round 2 (392fd563), matching the evidence note.

findings.desc: dispatch-usage.ts:199 + streaming.ts container reads — the CONTAINER read is unguarded: extractAnthropicUsage(envelope.usage) reads envelope.usage via prototype-chain BEFORE the in-function chokepoint; if Object.prototype.usage={input_tokens:999,...} and envelope lacks own usage, the inherited container object is passed in and its OWN props pass the whitelist. Same for streaming.ts stream containers (usage/usageMetadata). Fix: own-prop guard the container read (ownProp(envelope,'usage') / ownProp(container,'usage'|'usageMetadata')) before projecting; only treat an OWN-property container as present.
findings.resolvedReason: Round 2 (392fd563): own-prop guard every external container read (envelope.usage/model, stream usage/usageMetadata/message); inherited-only container treated absent. CONTAINER-POLLUTION smoke load-bearing.

findings.desc: assemble.ts:76 (sanitizeRawUsage) — BILLING/DIGEST REGRESSION for legitimate data: the projected whitelist-only object REPLACES the raw payload that flows to the adapter, and buildProviderReportedUsage computes raw.payloadDigest = sha256(canonicalJson(rawUsage)) over THAT projected object. So a normal un-polluted provider payload carrying legitimate extra fields the adapter does not read (openai total_tokens, gemini totalTokenCount, service_tier, nested non-read details) now produces a DIFFERENT payloadDigest than pre-hardening — a silent change to persisted records. Note canonicalJson uses Object.keys (own-only), so digesting the ORIGINAL raw payload is already pollution-safe AND preserves extra fields. Fix: compute payloadDigest from the ORIGINAL raw payload; use the projected/guarded object ONLY for the token-field READS (do not let projection feed the digest). Add a smoke: a legitimate payload WITH extra fields (total_tokens etc.) yields a payloadDigest byte-identical to pre-hardening.
findings.resolvedReason: Round 2 (392fd563): adapters digest the ORIGINAL raw payload (canonicalJson own-only), project only for reads; payloadDigest byte-identical for legit data incl extra fields. DIGEST-PRESERVED smoke.

findings.desc: quality-cleanup: dispatch-usage.ts:56 defines a local ANTHROPIC_USAGE_WHITELIST that duplicates the exported ANTHROPIC_USAGE_WHITELIST from adapters/anthropic.ts but does not import it — if the adapter whitelist ever gains or loses a field the dispatch extractAnthropicUsage path silently stays on the stale local copy
findings.resolvedReason: Round 3 (cb956812) / round 4 (6f719cd2): single shared whitelist — dispatch imports ANTHROPIC_USAGE_WHITELIST; streaming imports OPENAI/GEMINI whitelists from the adapters.

findings.desc: streaming.ts:231 (openai) + :285 (gemini) — STREAMING digest regression (same class as F-005, on the streaming path FIX A missed): the streaming extractor pre-projects the terminal stream usage via sanitizeOpenAiStreamUsage / toOwnPropsNullProto BEFORE calling adaptOpenAiUsage/adaptGeminiUsage, so the adapter digests the PROJECTION → legitimate extra fields (openai total_tokens / nested audio_tokens, gemini totalTokenCount) are dropped from raw.payloadDigest vs the original terminal usage payload. The pre-projection was added by THIS story (CHK-002), so it is a regression. Fix: digest the ORIGINAL terminal stream usage (own-prop-guarded container), project ONLY for the token reads — mirror FIX A. Add a streaming DIGEST-PRESERVED smoke (legit stream terminal usage WITH extra fields → payloadDigest === original).
findings.resolvedReason: Round 3 (cb956812): streaming openai/gemini digest the ORIGINAL terminal usage (pass original to adapter), project only for reads. Streaming DIGEST-PRESERVED smoke load-bearing.

findings.desc: dispatch-usage.ts:215 — resultText reads inherited envelope.result via prototype-chain; Object.prototype.result can replace the raw fallback text on a no-own-result envelope (same unguarded-container class as F-004, missed in round 2). Not a token surface, but same hardening class in the same file. Fix: own-prop guard the envelope.result read (ownProp(envelope,'result') ? ... : fallback). Add a smoke check that a polluted Object.prototype.result is not used when the envelope has no own result.

doc-promise-undelivered: streaming.ts block comment (lines 39-44) says the projection makes every downstream read INCLUDING the adapter call operate on a null-proto whitelist-only object, but after F-007 the adapter call receives the ORIGINAL (not the projection) — the comment was not updated and now actively misleads: it implies the adapter sees a projection when in reality the adapter does its own internal project-for-reads and digests the original

concept-cleanup: streaming.ts defines local OPENAI_STREAM_WHITELIST / OPENAI_STREAM_NESTED_DETAIL_WHITELIST / GEMINI_STREAM_WHITELIST as manual copies of the exported OPENAI_USAGE_WHITELIST / OPENAI_NESTED_DETAIL_WHITELIST / GEMINI_USAGE_WHITELIST from adapters/openai.ts and adapters/gemini.ts instead of importing them — the same DRY divergence risk that F-006 fixed for the anthropic whitelist in dispatch-usage.ts remains unaddressed for openai and gemini in streaming.ts; the misleading comment Enumerated directly from the adapters implies import not manual copy

record.ts validator still uses prototype-chain presence reads on the record being validated: :357 (required top-level fields), :369 (storyId in), :381 (supersedesRecordIds in), :527 (optional estimator.confidence in). The record input is internally assembled (lower risk than external JSON), but the story goal is a SYSTEMATIC sweep — leaving these inconsistent with the :493 conversion. Fix: convert ALL these to Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call (MECHANISM only; B-253e validation RULES unchanged), and grep the whole core/usage-ledger module to confirm NO 'key in obj' prototype-chain presence read remains (except genuinely-internal-table bracket lookups in diagnostics, which the spec marks optional). Add a smoke: pollute Object.prototype.storyId/supersedesRecordIds with a record MISSING that own field → validation still fails (load-bearing).
